hypotheses.statement: The concurrency increase from 8 to 32 workers caused database connection pool exhaustion because the pool size remained at 20
The expired service token caused settlement failures because the worker fails closed when it cannot read the settlement_v2_enabled flag
The two faults (pool exhaustion and token expiry) started independently four minutes apart and together caused the observed 61% failure rate
Some settlement attempts experienced both pool_timeout and token rejection failures simultaneously

observed_facts.statement: The database connection pool size was left at 20 and is not derived from the worker count
The service token expiry at 15:59:00Z is unrelated to the concurrency change applied four minutes earlier at 15:55:00Z
Pool exhaustion affected approximately 0.38 of settlement attempts
Token rejection affected approximately 0.31 of settlement attempts, overlapping with pool_timeout failures on some attempts
The alert did not clear until 18:12:30Z
The ticket records no settlement value at risk and no such figure was added before resolution
The metrics series shows two distinct step changes in failure ratio, each aligned with a different remediation
Pool_timeout errors stopped when connection pool was raised to 64
401 responses stopped when replacement token was installed

open_questions.missing_evidence: Design documentation or configuration management rationale explaining the relationship between worker count and pool size
open_questions.question: Why is the database connection pool size not derived from the worker concurrency?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Inventory of service tokens with their issuance dates, expiry dates, and renewal automation status
open_questions.question: Which other service tokens are on manual renewal and may expire without automated detection?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Financial impact assessment or settlement value metrics during the incident window
open_questions.question: What was the settlement value at risk during the incident?

summary: Payment settlement failures occurred from 15:58Z to 18:12Z on 2026-02-11, reaching 61% failure rate. Two independent faults coincided: (1) database connection pool exhaustion after a worker concurrency increase, and (2) feature-flag service token expiry. The pool was exhausted because its size (20) was not increased with worker count (8→32). The token expiry caused authentication failures to the flags service. Remediation occurred in two steps: pool enlargement at 17:20Z reduced failures to 29%, and token replacement at 18:12Z resolved remaining failures.

timeline.statement: Configuration change raised settlement-worker concurrency from 8 to 32 workers
Database connection pool exhausted with pool size 20, checked-out 20, queue depth rising
Feature-flag service token expired (issued for 90 days on 2025-11-13)
Calls to flags.internal returning 401 invalid_token, worker fails closed when cannot read settlement_v2_enabled flag
Alert fired: settlement attempts failing reached 0.61 against objective of 0.02
INC-2201 opened with severity 1, title 'Settlements failing'
Connection pool raised to 64, pool_timeout errors stopped, failure ratio fell from 0.61 to 0.29
Responder noted pool is at 64 and pool_timeout is gone, but failures still at 29%
Responder identified two separate faults: pool exhaustion from concurrency change and token expiry
Replacement token installed for flags.internal, 401 responses stopped, failure ratio fell from 0.29 to 0.004
Responder noted remaining questions about why pool size is not derived from worker concurrency and which other service tokens are on manual renewal
